extracted.intended_audience: general readers seeking guidance on social manners, conversational skill, and literary taste (Victorian/19th-century readership)
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive guidance and evaluative criteria for novels, personal character, social etiquette, and the art of talk — advising how to behave, host, converse, and what makes literature and conversation valuable. Targets both personal conduct and the design of social gatherings and conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novels as journal or record of manners
rubrics_metrics.description: Novels are the journal or record of manners; their new importance derives from the fact that the novelist begins to penetrate the surface, and treats this part of life more worthily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good novels should move beyond vulgar, formulaic plots (e.g., rags-to-riches with wedding as sole aim) to present deeper treatment of social life and manners, enriching readers with ideas or virtuous impulses rather than merely sentimental outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novels should teach the value of conversation and confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The novels are as useful as Bibles, if they teach you the secret, that the best of life is conversation, and the greatest success is confidence, or perfect understanding between sincere people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A novel's moral or educative value lies in portraying and promoting sincere understanding between people ('rien que s'entendre') and mutual trust rather than superficial plot resolutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Character victories should be instant and enlarging
rubrics_metrics.description: But the victories of character are instant, and victories for all. Its greatness enlarges all. We are fortified by every heroic anecdote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narratives and real-life examples that show moral or heroic character acting decisively uplift readers broadly; good portrayals of character have immediate, universal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mutual understanding and loyalty in heroes
rubrics_metrics.description: That is the charm in all good novels, as it is the charm in all good histories, that the heroes mutually understand, from the first, and deal loyally, and with a profound trust in each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-drawn relationships where protagonists recognize and trust each other from the outset yield moral clarity and exemplify admirable social bonds; authors should emphasize sincerity and loyalty over contrived conflicts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Directness and truthfulness in superior persons
rubrics_metrics.description: In all the superior people I have met, I notice directness, truth spoken more truly, as if everything of obstruction, of malformation, had been trained away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal excellence shows as straightforward speech and transparency; characters (or people) without evasions or affectations are perceived as superior and form the basis of good social relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and uprightness over mere talent
rubrics_metrics.description: Between simple and noble persons, there is always a quick intelligence: they recognize at sight, and meet on a better ground than the talents and skills they may chance to possess, namely, on sincerity and uprightness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating character (in life or fiction), prioritize how one relates to their talents — their integrity and sincerity — rather than the mere possession of gifts or genius.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-control and a good heart beautify demeanor
rubrics_metrics.description: They must always show self-control: you shall not be facile, apologetic, or leaky, but king over your word; and every gesture and action shall indicate power at rest. Then they must be inspired by the good heart.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Polished manners combine restraint and benevolence: avoid excessive apologies or oversharing; display calm confidence and genuine wish to 'scatter joy and not pain' to beautify appearance and conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid discussing one's ailments in company
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one topic peremptorily forbidden to all well-bred, to all rational mortals, namely, their distempers. If you have not slept, or if you have slept, or if you have headache... I beseech you ... to hold your peace, and not pollute the morning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As a social rule, refrain from bringing personal physical complaints into convivial company; doing so poisons the group mood and is considered ill-bred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Culture: rely on negative rules and natural inspiration
rubrics_metrics.description: As respects the delicate question of culture, I do not think that any other than negative rules can be laid down. For positive rules, for suggestion, nature alone inspires it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prescriptive checklists for cultivating manners; instead, remove faults (negative rules) and allow natural good taste and temperament to guide positive expression; be wary of trying to 'sketch' perfect conduct artificially.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legitimate restraints vs. factitious conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: By adding to the legitimate restraints, which are based on convenience and a regard for others, a host of factitious restraints based only on convention, the refining discipline ... is rendered unbearable, and so misses its end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Retain rules grounded in practical courtesy and consideration; discard arbitrary conventions that burden participants and defeat the purpose of refinement (mutual ease and moral culture).

rubrics_metrics.name: Informal, impromptu gatherings yield deeper pleasure
rubrics_metrics.description: Who, on calling to mind the occasions of his highest social enjoyments, does not find them to have been wholly informal, perhaps impromptu? How delightful a picnic of friends ... purely accidental meetings ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When organizing or valuing social events, prioritize spontaneous, informal assemblies where participants are at ease; these settings encourage liveliness, sincere feeling, and authentic exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive preparation and formality diminish enjoyment
rubrics_metrics.description: By the time we have got ready our elaborate apparatus by which to secure happiness, the happiness is gone... The more we multiply and complicate appliances, the more certain are we to drive it away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid over-planning and ornamental preparations (strict dress codes, elaborate ceremonies) that distract attention and reduce the chance of spontaneous pleasure; simplicity often preserves the emotion sought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on essentials, avoid multiplying non-essentials
rubrics_metrics.description: The more multiplied the unnecessary requirements with which social intercourse is surrounded, the less likely are its pleasures to be achieved... The attempt inevitably ends in the sacrifice of the first to the last--the essentials to the non-essentials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and maintain the core conditions for convivial communion (sympathy, ease, readiness to listen); minimize needless rules that divert attention and create occasions for misunderstanding or jealousy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for sympathetic converse where face and voice speak
rubrics_metrics.description: Some sympathetic converse with our fellow-creatures: some converse that shall not be mere dead words, but the vehicle of living thoughts and feelings--converse in which the eyes and the face shall speak, and the tones of the voice be full of meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality social interaction values nonverbal cues and heartfelt expression; conversation should be living and expressive, not perfunctory exchanges about topicalities without feeling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assemble intimate circles rather than large mixed gatherings
rubrics_metrics.description: A rationally-formed circle must consist almost wholly of those on terms of familiarity and regard, with but one or two strangers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For genuine communion, curate guest lists to include primarily familiar people; limit numbers and strangers to foster true intimacy and meaningful exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal gatherings often serve secondary, instrumental ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Worthless for their ostensible purpose of daily bringing human beings into pleasurable relations with each other, these cumbrous appliances of our social intercourse are now perseveringly kept in action with a view to the pecuniary and matrimonial results which they indirectly produce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be critical of social rituals that persist primarily for networking, advancement, or transactional ends rather than for pleasure and moral cultivation; recognize when etiquette serves other interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reform etiquette when observances become obstructive
rubrics_metrics.description: Forms that have ceased to facilitate and have become obstructive ... have ever to be swept away ... The fundamental change ... is not the replacing of absurd usages by sensible ones, but the dethronement of that secret, irresponsible power which now imposes our usages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support simplifying and democratizing social customs when they calcify into a tyrannical standard; the aim is to restore individual freedom of choice in modes of living rather than simply substituting one arbitrary code for another.

rubrics_metrics.name: Individual nonconformity often needs collective action
rubrics_metrics.description: The influence of dissentients acting without cooperation, seems, under the present state of things, inadequate ... The failure of individual nonconformity to customs ... suggests that an analogous series of changes may have to be gone through ... it may possibly be that nothing effectual will be done until there arises some organised resistance ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking to change harmful social conventions, understand the limits of solitary protest; collective, organized alternatives and mutual support are more likely to effect enduring change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ambition to excel in talk: be affable, ready, and welcome
rubrics_metrics.description: There can be no fairer ambition than to excel in talk; to be affable, gay, ready, clear and welcome; to have a fact, a thought, or an illustration, pat to every subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to be pleasant, prepared with apt material, and adaptable in conversation; successful talkers combine cordial manner with readiness and clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk is tentative, fluid, and different from written prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Talk is fluid, tentative, continually 'in further search and progress;' while written words remain fixed, become idols ... Talk goes fancy free and may call a spade a spade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use talk for exploratory, immediate exchange; favor spontaneity and adaptability rather than the fixedness and formality of written expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good talk arises when hour, company, and circumstance suit
rubrics_metrics.description: A good talk is not to be had for the asking. Humours must first be accorded in a kind of overture or prologue; hour, company and circumstance be suited; and then, at a fit juncture, the subject ... springs up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to situational readiness: the right mood, participants, and timing are prerequisites for lively, rewarding conversation; cultivate the setting as much as the content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Natural talk should be brief, instance-driven, and apposite
rubrics_metrics.description: Natural talk, like ploughing, should turn up a large surface of life, rather than dig mines into geological strata. Such argument as is proper to the exercise should still be brief and seizing. Talk should proceed by instances; by the apposite, not the expository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor vivid anecdotes, varied experience, and brief, pointed remarks over long expositions; use examples and cross-lights to enliven conversation and keep it accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use diverse material: anecdote, incident, quotation, cross-lights
rubrics_metrics.description: Masses of experience, anecdote, incident, cross-lights, quotation, historical instances ... these are the material with which talk is fortified, the food on which the talkers thrive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare and draw on a wide range of small materials — stories, quotations, historical instances — to sustain engaging, multifaceted talk; breadth of material supports lively exchange.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trust to hazard and follow the conversation's flow
rubrics_metrics.description: The genuine artist follows the stream of conversation as an angler follows the windings of a brook, not dallying where he fails to 'kill.' He trusts implicitly to hazard; and he is rewarded by continual variety, continual pleasure ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be adaptive and willing to take conversational risks; follow promising tangents and withdraw from dead tracks rather than forcing topics — good talkers read the 'bite' and move accordingly.
